newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong property stocks continue recovery.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong property stocks continue recovery.

text.p: Hong Kong property stocks led the market higher in Thursday morning trade, lifted by new optimism on the interest rate outlook and recovery-play opportunities, brokers and analysts said.
"The (real estate) developers are still in recovery," said Janet Gillies, sales director at OCBC Securities.
The property sub-index was trading 427.57 points, or 1.87 percent, higher at 23,325.85 in mid-morning trade, compared with the Hang Seng Index's 0.42 percent gain.
The sector index is still more than 4,000 points off its all time high of 27,411.54, set on November 28, 1996.
The sector was boosted by overnight gains on Wall Street and by the rising U.S. long bond, whose yield fell to 6.95 percent.
Developers led the poperty sector up, while property investment companies languished with minor gains.
Developer Sun Hung Kai Properties led the sector with a jump of HK$2.00 to HK$86.00. New World Development followed with a gain of HK$1.60 to HK46.30.

"The share is trading at a reasonable discount to its NAV (net asset value), said Terry Yip, property analyst at BZW Securities. "As a house we favour New World (Development), Cheung Kong and Sino Land."

Sino Land put on HK$0.50, or 6.80 percent, to HK$7.85. The company recently announced that it would sell the next batch of residential apartments in its Waterside complex at higher prices, at an average HK$6,253 per square foot.
"Cheung Kong's chart looks good," said Gillies. "It looks like it will go to HK$72.00 in the short term."
Cheung Kong added HK$1.50, or 2.21 percent, to HK$69.50 on moderate turnover of HK$162.18 million.
Property investor Amoy Properties added HK$0.10 to HK$7.75.
